audience: people who design and rank feeds
title: Engagement Is the User Trying to Leave
subtitle: A simulated study of feedback in ranked feeds: every control the user touches becomes content, and the ranking buries what she came for
premise: Ranked feeds record every user action and feed it back as signal. We simulate a feed with the ordinary machinery, a ranking that favours what asks something of the user, a cut-off, a lifetime, bursts of arrivals, and a learning loop on likes, hides and mutes, and measure what the user's own tidying does to the feed and to four modelled dimensions of the user.
claim: Under engagement-weighted ranking, the user's controls increase the share of the feed that is her own echo; muting makes room but does not choose what fills it; liking what she wanted is the only control that works in her favour, and it too comes back as content; and stopping does not clear anything.
applicability: A control that is logged as engagement is a control that increases the feed's hold; the design question is which controls should not be signal.
The ranking asymmetry is a tunable in this model; it is the constant to contest, and the lab exposes it in one file.
Stopping dilutes rather than removes: a feed that wants to be left alone should expire the user's echoes faster than the stream.
tone: precise, mechanistic; name the control, the constant and the number
